stories.title: IndiGo flight returns to Pune after landing gear snag
stories.summary: An IndiGo flight carrying 192 people returned to Pune on Sunday after its landing gear failed to retract shortly after takeoff. The Indian Air Force, which manages the airport, declared a full emergency. The aircraft landed safely, and emergency response teams were stood down shortly after.

stories.title: Emirates leans into premium economy on Dubai routes
stories.summary: Emirates is rolling out premium economy across its fleet, a cabin class not currently offered by regional rivals Etihad and Qatar Airways. The airline maintains a focus on premium seating, including first class on nearly all aircraft, to capture demand on longer international routes.

stories.title: Malaysia Airlines to install lie-flat seats on narrowbody jets
stories.summary: Malaysia Airlines plans to introduce lie-flat business-class seats on its Boeing 737 MAX 10 aircraft. While such seating is typically reserved for widebody jets on long-haul routes, the carrier believes the configuration will provide a competitive advantage in regional Asia-Pacific markets.

stories.title: Delta launches nine-hour seasonal route to Maui
stories.summary: Delta Air Lines has launched a seasonal nonstop route between Minneapolis and Maui. The carrier is using an Airbus A330-300 for the nine-hour flight, citing the route as a previously unserved market that saw 66,000 indirect passengers annually. The service is scheduled to run until mid-April.

stories.title: United Airlines doubles frequencies on seven Denver routes
stories.summary: United Airlines is doubling flight frequencies on seven routes from its Denver hub for summer 2027. The airline operates over 500 daily flights from the Colorado airport, which currently ranks as its second-busiest hub by passenger volume and available seats, according to Cirium data.

stories.title: RwandAir expands fleet with classic Airbus A330s
stories.summary: RwandAir has begun an expansion program adding five classic Airbus A330-200 aircraft to its fleet. While the industry often prioritizes newer, re-engined models, the airline is opting for established widebodies to support a commercial push for regional connectivity and high-yield traffic.

stories.title: American Airlines maintains Boeing 787 fleet strategy
stories.summary: The Airbus A350 is widely recognized for its range and composite construction, leading many international carriers to integrate the model into long-term plans. American Airlines remains a notable exception, opting to focus its widebody operations on the Boeing 787 instead.

stories.title: Qatar Airways trims Belgrade and Zagreb plans, eyes Sarajevo return
stories.summary: Qatar Airways is adjusting its regional network by reducing planned services to Belgrade and Zagreb while exploring a potential return to Sarajevo. The airline has not provided further details on the schedule changes or the timeline for resuming operations in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

stories.title: Emirates balances A350 fleet with Boeing 777X orders
stories.summary: Emirates operates an all-widebody fleet of over 250 aircraft, including 30 Airbus A350-900s with 43 more on order. Despite the A350's popularity in the widebody market, the airline has also committed to the Boeing 777X to support its long-haul operations.

stories.title: Airlines report fleet, cabin and route changes
stories.summary: Lufthansa has taken delivery of its first A350-1000, while the Cathay Group has ordered 14 additional Airbus aircraft. The industry updates also include Korean Air’s planned Seoul-Incheon-Newark route and the installation of Starlink Wi-Fi on Iberia’s A321XLR fleet.

stories.title: Delta Air Lines replaces aging A319s with A220s
stories.summary: Delta Air Lines has ordered 145 Airbus A220s to replace its aging A319 fleet. While American and United also operate the A319, neither carrier has placed orders for the A319neo, A220, or equivalent narrowbody replacements to modernize their current operations.

stories.title: Global Airlines enters compulsory liquidation
stories.summary: Global Airlines has been ordered into compulsory liquidation following a court-issued winding-up order on November 4. The company's primary asset, a single Airbus A380 currently in long-term storage, is expected to be sold by court-appointed liquidators to satisfy outstanding debts.

stories.title: Global Airlines faces liquidation after operating four flights
stories.summary: British startup Global Airlines has been ordered into compulsory liquidation by a UK court. The company, which aimed to operate a fleet of Airbus A380s, faced the order 18 months after completing its only commercial flights. It never established a regular service.

stories.title: Boeing sells aerospace units to Archer Aviation
stories.summary: Boeing is selling three aerospace businesses to Archer Aviation, providing the electric aircraft developer with an established defense operation. Simultaneously, Boeing secured a $131.23 billion U.S. military contract for its F-15 fighter jet program to simplify its own operations.

stories.title: Cathay Group expands Airbus fleet
stories.summary: Cathay Group has ordered 14 additional Airbus aircraft, including 11 A330-900s and three A321neos. This purchase raises the group's committed investment between 2026 and 2035 to more than HK$150 billion as part of its fleet modernization and expansion strategy.

stories.title: Cathay Group orders 14 additional Airbus aircraft
stories.summary: The Cathay Group has placed a firm order for 14 Airbus aircraft, consisting of 11 A330-900s and three A321neos. The airline states the new aircraft will improve regional and long-haul operations while supporting sustainability objectives through reduced fuel consumption.

stories.title: Germany moves toward A400M transport aircraft order
stories.summary: The Bundestag Budget Committee has approved amendments to the 2027 defense budget, clearing a path for Germany to acquire 16 additional Airbus A400M transport aircraft. The tactical-configuration jets are intended for use in high-threat environments. The purchase is not yet a firm order.

stories.title: Germany plans 16 new A400M airlifters
stories.summary: Germany intends to purchase 16 additional Airbus A400M transport aircraft in a tactical configuration. The German Defense Ministry stated the move provides new work for the production line, which is currently facing a shrinking order backlog.

stories.title: Saudi THC confirms Bombardier order for 12 business jets
stories.summary: The Helicopter Company has finalized a binding order for 12 Bombardier business jets, including five Challenger 3500s, five Global 5500s, and two Global 8000s. The deal is valued at approximately $568 million and includes options for 48 additional aircraft.

stories.title: Lufthansa receives 700th Airbus delivery
stories.summary: Lufthansa has taken delivery of its first A350-1000, marking the 700th Airbus aircraft delivered to the Lufthansa Group. The jet features the new Allegris cabin and will operate on long-haul routes from Munich to Tokyo, Shanghai, and Singapore.

stories.title: Boeing orders rise as deliveries decline
stories.summary: Boeing recorded 165 aircraft orders in October, its strongest performance since 1997, largely driven by an Avolon order. However, monthly deliveries fell to 49 jets, down from 57 in September. The company reported no cancellations during the period.

stories.title: Ground stop issued at Orlando International Airport
stories.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration issued a ground stop at Orlando International Airport on Sunday following an emergency involving Southwest Flight 2879. The aircraft landed safely after returning to the airport shortly after departure. The cause of the issue remains undisclosed.

stories.title: Federal aviation officials repeatedly warned about potential risks in rushing modernization of national air traffic cont
FAA investigates radar sites following ground stop
stories.summary: The FAA is investigating a radar site in Amarillo, Texas, and a radio communications site in Arkansas as potential sources of data flooding that caused a nationwide ground stop on Friday. L3Harris, the network provider, blocked both locations to stabilize the network.

stories.title: FAA investigates cause of nationwide ground stop
stories.summary: A nationwide ground stop halted U.S. air travel for nearly five hours on Friday after radar and radio feeds experienced intermittent failures. The FAA is currently investigating whether technical issues at radar and communications sites in Texas and Arkansas caused the network overload.

stories.title: Atlanta airport reports hundreds of delays after FAA ground stop
stories.summary: Hartsfield-Jackson International Airport reported 644 flight delays and 134 cancellations on Sunday, two days after a nationwide FAA ground stop. Delta Air Lines accounted for 461 of the delayed flights. The FAA attributed the initial disruption to routine maintenance performed by a contractor.

stories.title: FAA investigates Texas radar site for data flooding
stories.summary: The FAA is investigating a Remote Center Air/Ground Communication site in Amarillo, Texas, as a potential source of the data flooding that triggered Friday's nationwide ground stop. The unmanned facility is operated remotely by the Albuquerque Center. The agency has not yet confirmed the site as the culprit.

stories.title: Montreal airport operations return to normal
stories.summary: Operations at Montreal-Trudeau International Airport were described as much more regular on Sunday following the nationwide U.S. aviation shutdown on Friday. An Aéroports de Montréal spokesperson stated that the facility is now pretty much back to normal. Recovery efforts continued throughout the weekend.

stories.title: Trump calls for air traffic control funding
stories.summary: President Donald Trump called for increased funding to upgrade the air traffic control system following the nationwide ground stop. He claimed that approved money would allow the government to build the best system in the world quickly and efficiently. The statement followed two days of silence.

stories.title: Boise Airport reports lingering flight disruptions
stories.summary: Travelers at Boise Airport continued to experience delays and cancellations on Sunday, two days after the FAA ground stop halted all flights for four hours. The airport recorded 41 delays and seven cancellations. Passengers have been advised to contact their airlines directly for updated flight status information.

stories.title: Audio reveals radio issues preceded FAA ground stop
stories.summary: Air traffic controllers in Fresno reported radio frequency problems approximately 40 minutes before the FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop on Friday. Audio recordings show controllers struggling to communicate with aircraft and switching frequencies. A warning about a potential ground stop was issued shortly thereafter.

Flight disruptions persist across the United States
Piper Aircraft signs deal with Alpha Aviation Group
stories.summary: Piper Aircraft will supply Alpha Aviation Group with six Archer DX aircraft by the end of 2026. The agreement is part of a broader push to expand pilot training in Southeast Asia, with Piper eyeing a total of more than 100 aircraft for the group's training programs.

stories.title: ThePilot.in and US Aviation Academy announce training webinar
stories.summary: Indian training facilitator ThePilot.in will host a webinar on November 25, 2026, featuring the US Aviation Academy. The event aims to introduce Indian students to flight training opportunities in Florida, including a 12-month commercial pilot pathway and information on student housing options.

stories.title: Bihar secures clearance for Darbhanga pilot training facility
stories.summary: The Government of Bihar has received defense clearance to establish a Flying Training Organisation at Darbhanga Airport. The project, which received a No Objection Certificate from the Ministry of Defence in September, aims to increase commercial pilot training capacity in northern India pending further regulatory approvals.

stories.title: Mexican flight school installs Airbus A320 simulator
stories.summary: Escuela de Vuelo Aeronáutica Vitar has installed an Airbus A320 cockpit simulator manufactured by Italy-based CPflight. The equipment is intended to provide students with a dedicated environment for systems instruction and procedural training. CPflight has over 25 years of experience in developing flight simulation hardware.

stories.title: FlyBy Aviation Academy welcomes final 2026 cadet intake
stories.summary: FlyBy Aviation Academy in Spain has inducted 52 new cadets, marking its final intake for 2026. The EASA-approved organization operates training programs at Burgos and Logroño-Agoncillo airports. The academy is now preparing its professional pilot training pipeline for the 2027 calendar year.
